description_long.current: Court documents filed in August 2026 disclosed undercover Department of Homeland Security activity aimed at organizations and people protesting the immigration crackdown in Minneapolis. The New Republic, the Associated Press and other outlets reported that agents attended meetings, entered Signal chats, recorded some gatherings and sought financial records from groups including the Sunrise Movement, the Service Employees International Union and the Communications Workers of America. One set of documents described an undercover agent at a January 31 Sunrise Movement meeting in a public library, where participants discussed peaceful protest tactics and safety measures. The activity began after federal agents fatally shot Renee Good and Alex Pretti during the enforcement operation, intensifying protests and scrutiny of federal policing. Prosecutors had charged a number of activists in a separate case; defense attorneys attached the investigative reports to court filings and challenged the government’s portrayal of a broader conspiracy. The records raised concerns about surveillance of protected speech and association, particularly where groups or attendees were not accused of crimes. DHS’s stated investigative rationale and the full legal basis for each subpoena remain contested. The documents demonstrate surveillance of identified groups in Minnesota, but they do not by themselves establish a single nationwide program or that President Trump personally directed the operations. The title’s original “secret police” phrase was an editorial characterization and is not used as a factual label.
